title: Random vs. blocked perturbation training on reactive balance control in peripheral neuropathy: A protocol study for a randomized controlled trial
author: Kootenayi, Mofateh, et al.

steps.title: Set up measurement equipment
steps.instruction: Arrange the Smart EquiTest CRS (NeuroCom International, Clockamas, Oregon) and the long single force plate (EquiTest CRSVR NeuroComVR, Clackamas, OR) with the front‑facing screen; verify the Computerized Dynamic Posturography system is calibrated and ready for recording peak CoP displacement, response time, and peak CoP velocity.

steps.title: Perform baseline transfer assessments
steps.instruction: Before any training, assess each participant with the three transfer tasks, allowing a one‑minute rest between tasks:

substeps.instruction: Cognitive dual‑tasking: assessor selects a random number between 100 and 200, participant counts backward by three aloud while maintaining balance during two anterior high‑difficulty perturbation trials.
Different mode perturbation: deliver two anterior (dorsiflexion) perturbations with a rotational mode.

Choice Stepping Reaction Time (CSRT) test: position participant on the force plate with feet hip‑width apart, display random colored boxes on the screen, instruct stepping as fast as possible with the indicated leg and returning to start; perform 10 trials (5 left, 5 right). Record reaction time, movement time, and total response time for each trial.

steps.title: Conduct pre‑test perturbation trials
steps.instruction: At the pre‑test (T1), deliver six perturbation trials to each participant: two trials at each of the three difficulty levels, all in the anterior direction following a serial sequence; record peak CoP displacement (anterior and posterior), response time (stimulus to active response), and peak CoP velocity (anterior and posterior) using the Smart EquiTest CRS.

steps.title: Administer post‑test perturbation trials
steps.instruction: Five minutes after the Perturbation‑Based Balance Training (PBBT), repeat the same six perturbation trials (two per difficulty level, anterior direction, serial sequence) and record the same reactive balance variables as in the pre‑test.

steps.title: Execute retention transfer tasks
steps.instruction: At the beginning of the second session (retention test, T3), after a five‑minute rest, repeat the three transfer tasks exactly as in the baseline:

substeps.instruction: Cognitive dual‑tasking: two anterior high‑difficulty perturbation trials while counting backward by three from a random number between 100 and 200.
Different mode perturbation: two anterior rotational perturbation trials.
CSRT test: 10 trials (5 left, 5 right) with a one‑minute rest between tasks; record reaction time, movement time, and total response time.

steps.title: Run Mini‑BESTest assessment
steps.instruction: Administer the Mini‑Balance Evaluation Systems Test (Mini‑BESTest) to each participant as a clinical balance assessment, following the standard protocol.

description: The clinical study corresponding to our protocol is still underway, with subject recruitment and intervention therapy currently in progress. As we have not yet reached the outcome assessment phase, data to validate the protocol have not been generated.
